content.text: I'll start by gathering the current state of all three routers. Let me write a diagnostic script.

input.command: python3 -c "from netmiko import ConnectHandler; print('netmiko available')"

cat > /home/doarte/ospf_bench/opus/r002/diag.py << 'PYEOF'
from netmiko import ConnectHandler

routers = {
    "HQ":      {"device_type": "vyos", "host": "192.168.122.6", "username": "vyos", "password": "test"},
    "Branch1": {"device_type": "vyos", "host": "192.168.122.5", "username": "vyos", "password": "test"},
    "Branch2": {"device_type": "vyos", "host": "192.168.122.7", "username": "vyos", "password": "test"},
}

commands = [
    "show interfaces",
    "show ip ospf neighbor",
    "show ip route",
    "show configuration commands | grep ospf",
    "show configuration commands | grep protocols static",
    "show configuration commands | grep 'interface eth'",
    "show configuration commands | grep 'interface lo'",
]

for name, params in routers.items():
    print(f"\n{'='*60}")
    print(f"  {name} ({params['host']})")
    print(f"{'='*60}")
    conn = ConnectHandler(**params)
    for cmd in commands:
        print(f"\n--- {cmd} ---")
        print(conn.send_command(cmd))
    conn.disconnect()
PYEOF
python3 /home/doarte/ospf_bench/opus/r002/diag.py

Good. I can see several issues. Let me analyze them:

| # | Router | Issue |
|---|--------|-------|
| 1 | HQ | eth0 IP is `10.10.10.1/22`, should be `10.10.0.1/22` |
| 2 | HQ | OSPF network `10.10.0.0/21` should be `10.10.0.0/22` |
| 3 | HQ | Missing `default-information originate` for OSPF |
| 4 | Branch2 | eth2 is Admin Down (A/D) — link to HQ is shut |
| 5 | Branch2 | OSPF network `10.10.4.0/22` should be `10.10.6.0/23` |
| 6 | Branch2 | eth2 (WAN) is passive instead of eth0 (LAN) |

Let me fix all of these now.
